transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess what finally pushed me to come in is that I keep getting up in situations where I know I’m supposed to stay put. Like during sprint planning at work, or even mortgage calls, I’ll suddenly need water or decide I should check something in the other room. It’s not a huge dramatic thing, but it keeps happening and it’s starting to feel noticeable.
When that happens, are you mainly leaving because you feel afraid people are noticing or judging you?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I’m aware it probably looks a little odd sometimes, but it doesn’t feel like I’m leaving because I’m scared people are judging me. It’s more like I just… get up before I’ve really thought it through.
Before you get up, do you usually have a repeated unwanted thought or urge that feels like you need to act on it to feel better?

Not really, no. I don’t usually have some specific thought repeating in my head, or a feeling like I have to do it to make the thought stop. It’s more just sudden, like I’m already moving before I’ve really decided to.
Did you have this same tendency to act before thinking or get up and move around when you were a child?

Yes, I think so. I remember in elementary school teachers would move my desk or remind me to stay seated because I was always popping up. I’d also talk before I was called on, or rush through assignments even when I actually understood the work. It wasn’t constant trouble or anything, but it was definitely a pattern.
Have you ever had a period where your mood was unusually high or irritable for several days in a row?

I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve had a stretch like that, where my mood was really unusually high for days. I can get irritable sometimes, but I haven’t noticed it lasting several days in a row in a way that felt out of character.
When you get up in those situations, is it usually because you’re feeling worried or keyed up?

Not usually worried, no. It’s more like this internal restlessness. Even if I look like I’m sitting calmly, inside I feel this pressure to move or switch tasks or do something with my hands, otherwise I start feeling like I’m crawling out of my skin.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different parts of your life, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?
I don’t think so. I mean, I worry about normal things like work or bills sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I spend a lot of time worrying about everything when there’s no clear reason.
